method: Qualitative review of generated planning text and existing speaker ASR only; not a human audio blind evaluation

cases.finding: Base under swapped audio reproduces much of speaker utterance about homelessness; SFT examples instead remain in listener-style descriptions. A concrete role-control benefit, not overall preference proof.
SFT2752 text changes after swapping audio, but both descriptions essentially remain neutral, blink, nod toward end, silent. Literal changes need not be meaningful planning changes.

Speaker context changes from discussing fatherhood to ordering coffee; SFT2752 plan is exactly unchanged including0.4s and1.8–2.4s nod timing. Demonstrates generic reuse on this case, not a universal error or proof of ignoring audio.

conclusion: SFT2752 has the highest literal audio-swap sensitivity in this subset; no semantic accuracy ranking or optimal training-budget conclusion is established.
